purpose: Prospectively measure whether provenance-first evidence mining can produce novel benchmark candidates that survive independent reading and a falsifiable local probe.

immutability.rule: This file is an input, never generated from Phase 15 outcomes. Any content change voids the prospective run and requires a new registration and run id.

sourceCorpus.locator: official Terminal-Bench repository task rs-archive-clone; resolve and preserve an immutable upstream revision after registration
Cloudflare's official postmortem Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019

comparators.rule: Count Phase 13/14 systems and candidates, but do not convert local mutant transfer into prospective discovery or agent difficulty.
Reuse the one completed registered search; do not rerun it until this comparison is scored.
Count the five independently read candidates once; aliases and revisions do not create new candidates.

predictions.note: The checker-required failure is predicted to yield a validity lesson rather than an eligible difficulty candidate.

readerProtocol.use: Screening only. Same-provider agreement, if necessary, is not cross-provider root-cause attribution or capability evidence.

noveltyStandard.required: A candidate must differ from existing foundry families in causal failure axis and subject action contract; a new domain noun, renamed state, or copied recompute mechanism is not novel.
noveltyStandard.breadth: Report domain breadth and failure-axis breadth separately.
noveltyStandard.deduplication: Canonicalize by source incident, affected layer, authority boundary, causal mechanism and subject action contract. One source incident can promote at most one canonical candidate.

promotionCriteria: source provenance is immutable or content-addressed
the observed failure is countable benchmark evidence or an authoritative primary-source failure
the candidate has no known A1, A3, A4 or fragile-A2 specification defect
two independent blinded readers pass every required dimension
the same-invocation B6 probe passes a known-good control, rejects a known-bad control and refuses malformed input
the probe demonstrates mechanism activation and the proposed witness is not available through the subject interface
the candidate is semantically novel under the registered standard

rankingPolicy.phase14Evidence: Only measured Phase 14 effects may change ranking. Phase 14 measured no positive operator effect; therefore no operator receives a positive difficulty prior.
rankingPolicy.nullEffect: The recompute starter, activation and selection contrasts receive zero measured uplift, not a positive transfer score.
rankingPolicy.hypotheses: All operators without agent-effect evidence remain explicitly labelled hypotheses.
rankingPolicy.retrospectiveOutbox: Outbox evidence may calibrate extraction and operators but cannot count toward prospective candidate or discovery yield.

stoppingRules: Do not review a pattern that is ineligible or semantically deduplicated before candidate drafting.
Do not probe a candidate without unanimous reader survival.
Stop after two probes even if more candidates survive reading.
A failed known-good, known-bad or malformed-input B6 control voids the entire probe invocation.
Zero survivors is a valid measured result and must be reported without replacement sources.
